transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what brought you in to see me today?

Hi, um… I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that I keep forgetting these little everyday things I’m usually on top of. Like returning phone calls, or I forgot to turn in a registration form—stuff like that. And then I’ll mean to stop for an errand on the way home and just completely drive past it. It’s not huge things, but it’s been happening enough that I thought maybe I should talk to someone.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?

Um… not really, I don’t think so. I mean, I have days where I’m tired or kind of frustrated, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling sad all the time or not enjoying things. Like, I still want to do my usual stuff when I actually get around to it. Sorry, I know that’s not a very straight answer.
Have you noticed yourself worrying a lot, more than usual, about various things in your daily life over the past several months?

Um… worrying a lot? I don’t know. I mean, I worry about normal stuff, like whether I paid a bill or if I’m late for something, but I wouldn’t say it’s more than usual. It’s more like I realize I forgot something and then I get annoyed with myself. Actually, the other day I was thinking about groceries and then remembered I never called my cousin back—sorry, that’s kind of not what you asked. But no, I haven’t really noticed constant worrying about a bunch of things.
Would you say this kind of forgetfulness has been part of how you've always been, even back in school or your 20s, or is this a new change you've noticed recently?

Yeah, I think it’s kind of always been there, honestly. Like even in elementary school I was the kid who’d forget permission slips, or I’d have homework done but then somehow lose it in my backpack. My mom or my teacher would have to remind me step by step to finish projects—like, “do this part, now this part.” I remember my backpack being this disaster of crumpled papers… and then I’d find something weeks later. So it feels familiar, not totally new.
Can you tell me how this forgetfulness has affected different areas of your life—like at work, at home, and in your relationships?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still functioning. It’s not like everything is falling apart. But at work, I’ll miss little follow-ups sometimes, like I’ll tell someone I’ll send something or check on something and then it just kind of disappears from my brain until later. And then I feel embarrassed because I’m a secretary, so I’m supposed to be on top of those details.

At home it’s more annoying than anything, like things piling up or forgetting something I meant to handle. And with relationships, I guess people can get frustrated if I don’t get back to them when I meant to.

The thing I worry about most is work, honestly. I’ve been hoping maybe I could move into more of an Office Manager role eventually, but when I miss small deadlines or follow-ups, I worry people see me as unreliable, even though I’m trying.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still, or find yourself blurting things out or acting impulsively in conversations or decisions?

Um… I don’t think I really blurt things out much, or at least I don’t notice that as a big thing. Restless, maybe a little? Like during longer classes or meetings—I know you said conversations, but it makes me think of sitting in those long trainings—I’ll catch myself clicking my pen, bouncing my foot, shifting around in the chair, even when I’m trying to sit still and pay attention.

It’s not like I’m jumping out of my seat or anything. It’s more just… I can’t seem to be totally still for that long.
Do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks or conversations, like your mind drifting off or getting distracted by things going on around you, even when you're trying to pay attention?

Yeah, definitely. Like at work, if the phone rings or people are talking near my desk, I can be in the middle of something and suddenly I’m following that instead of what I was doing. Or even in a class or training, my brain will wander off because I remember something random I need to do at home, like laundry or paying a bill, and then I’ve missed part of what was being said.

It’s frustrating because I am trying to pay attention, but it doesn’t always take much to pull me away.
Thinking back to before you turned 12 years old, were you already showing these same kinds of forgetfulness, distractibility, and restlessness at that age?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, it’s hard to remember everything from that age, but even in elementary school I was kind of that kid who forgot the permission slip until the morning it was due, or I’d swear I did my homework and then it was just lost somewhere in my backpack.

My mom had to remind me a lot, like one step at a time, to finish projects. And teachers too sometimes. I remember those big poster board projects—actually I always liked picking the colors and making them look nice, but the actual finishing part was where I’d sort of get lost unless someone kept nudging me. So yeah, I think it was there pretty early.
Have you noticed any issues with your sleep, like not getting enough rest, or do you use caffeine, alcohol, or other substances regularly that might be affecting your concentration?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed a clear pattern, like “oh, I slept badly so now I can’t concentrate,” but I guess I don’t always pay close attention to that kind of thing.

I mean, sleep is… normal-ish? Some nights are better than others. And caffeine, I’ll have some, like coffee or whatever, but I haven’t really thought of it as the reason. Alcohol or other stuff… I don’t know, nothing that really stands out to me as affecting it.

Sorry, I’m kind of answering around it. I guess the honest answer is I haven’t noticed anything obvious there.
